title: Taiwan's musical garbage trucks and the keep-trash-off-the-ground collection system

sources.title: Taiwan's garbage trucks offer classical music and a catch-up (2025-07-29)
sources.license: Taipei Times terms of use (facts only)

facts.text: Garbage trucks in Taiwan play Beethoven's Für Elise or Tekla Badarzewska-Baranowska's A Maiden's Prayer to tell residents to bring out their trash.
According to Taipei's Department of Environmental Protection, musical garbage trucks have been a near-daily part of life since the 1960s.
The trucks generally run five days a week, usually in the late afternoon and evening.
Residents take their pre-sorted trash out to the street when the truck arrives.
General waste goes into a yellow compactor truck, while food waste and recycling go into bins on a separate vehicle.
During a period of economic boom, Taiwan produced a surge of garbage, recycled little and saw landfills overflow.
The response included making residents sort their own trash and bring it to the trucks instead of leaving it on the ground.
Taipei residents must buy government-approved blue plastic bags for general waste.
Taipei's recycling rate is nearly 67 percent, up from 2 percent in 2000.
Many older residents arrive early at collection points to chat with neighbors, and some say the walk is good exercise.
Some residents find the fixed daily collection time inconvenient when they are busy or away from home.

notes: 音樂從何時、為何選這兩首曲子各來源說法不一，文章不寫起源細節。
